title: Reserved throughput contract template and automated risk-scorer for SLA commitments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose:
This ticket delivers two linked artifacts to standardize enterprise reserved-capacity intake and SLA negotiation: 1) a contract term template and decision checklist for reserved throughput/GPU commitments, and 2) an automated risk-scorer (rubric + spreadsheet) to objectively grade incoming requests against capacity, latency SLOs, GPU class, and burst/buffer policy.

Why this is needed:
We repeatedly spend engineering and sales cycles on bespoke SLA negotiations. Deals that accept stringent latency SLA on narrow GPU tiers or aggressive burst guarantees create disproportionate operational risk and cost. We need an intake artifact that (a) speeds negotiation by surfacing required technical inputs, (b) codifies fallback/buffer options when we can't meet requested targets, and (c) produces an objective risk score used in prioritization and pricing guidance.

Scope and deliverables:
- Contract template (DocX/Confluence): sections for throughput commitments, P99/P95 latency targets, GPU family and quantization allowances, burst policy, preemption/eviction terms, monitoring & alerting responsibilities, and clear consequences for exceeded utilization.
- Decision checklist (one-page): minimum signals we need from sales/SE (QPS profile, peak window, model family, max seq length, acceptable model variants, data residency).
- Automated risk-scorer (Google Sheet + scoring rules): numeric scoring of request along dimensions: utilization certainty (30%), latency tightness (25%), GPU sensitivity (15%), burstability (15%), and business criticality/SL (20%). Output is Low/Medium/High operational risk with suggested mitigations and a recommended pricing uplift band.
- Negotiation playbook: steps for PM/SE to follow when score is Medium/High, including standard fallbacks (reduced burst, higher GPU class, relaxed P99 with tail-latency mitigation using caching), and an escalation path to SRE/Capacity engineering.
- Example filled templates for three archetypes: SaaS PLG scale-up, enterprise regulated customer (HIPAA), and multi-region gaming workloads.

Out-of-scope:
- Implementation of billing engine changes.
- Automated enforcement in runtime. Those are follow-ups (ENG tickets).

Non-functional requirements:
- Template must be shareable as a single-page summary for legal and as a checklist for sales engineers.
- Risk-scorer must be deterministic and reproducible; all weights configurable in sheet.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract template available in Confluence with legal-approved placeholder clauses (string), and reviewed by Legal and Sales (one approval each).
- Risk-scorer sheet with documented formulae, a sample calculation for each archetype, and a short guidance note for score interpretation.
- Playbook contains 6-step negotiation flow with links to fallback templates (email snippets, config knobs to propose to customers).
- Three example filled intake forms attached and one mock Sales demo using the artifacts completed.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence contract template with Legal and Sales review comments resolved (review links present)
Risk-scorer Google Sheet with documented formulas and three sample scenarios
Negotiation playbook with explicit fallback options and escalation path to SRE
Three example intake forms: PLG SaaS, Regulated Enterprise, and Multi-region gaming
One mock negotiation run-through recorded and theta notes added to Confluence

2025-02-25 — Review with SRE: discussed feasibility of meeting 50ms P99 on A100 for 4k token workloads; SRE recommended explicit model-variant clause and a minimum GPU class table. Added GPU sensitivity weight to the scorer.
2025-02-28 — Legal provided placeholder warranty/limit-of-liability language. Added standard monitor-and-notify SLAs and breach remediation steps to contract template.

2025-03-03 — Prototype risk-scorer completed and tested against three historical enterprise requests (IDs: CUST-2334, CUST-1981, CUST-4177). Results attached; one case moved from High to Medium after proposing reduced burst and optional model quantization.
